I've been farming this same land in Quzhou for over 40 years. My father farmed it before me. I know what works here on the North China Plain — wheat in winter, corn in summer. That's what I'll do again this year, same as always. My two sons went to work in Shijiazhuang, so now I manage about 8 mu on my own. I don't want to risk trying something new at my age. The wheat-corn rotation keeps the soil decent, the buyers at the local grain station know what they're getting, and I know exactly what inputs I need.

For wheat, I'll plant in early October after the summer corn comes off. I use the Jimai variety — the seed station in the county town sells it and it does well here. I'll rotary-till after the corn harvest to chop up the stalks. I put down base fertilizer before planting — compound fertilizer plus urea — and I top-dress nitrogen at jointing. I irrigate four times: before winter sets in, at green-up, at jointing, and at grain fill. I spray for aphids and powdery mildew in spring, maybe twice. I expect around 450 jin per mu, so about 450 kg.

For summer corn, I plant right after wheat harvest in June — no time to waste. I use Xianyu 335 hybrid seed, been using it for years, reliable. I direct seed without tilling again. I put down a basal fertilizer and side-dress urea at the big bell stage. Corn here usually gets enough rain in July and August but I'll irrigate once or twice if it's dry. I spray for corn borer once. Should get 550 kg per mu if the rains cooperate.
